sources.note: Only two records: Glottolog 5.0 resources page and Ethnologue entry; no primary documentation archived anywhere in OLAC.

sources.citation: Ado, Zuwaira & Buhari Shehu Abubakar. 2020 [DOI registered 2026]. Lexicostatistics and Glottochronology in Lexical Analysis of Kuteb Dialects. Namoda Techscope (Federal Polytechnic Kaura Namoda) 12(1&2): 30-36. ISSN 1118-1672. DOI 10.63725/namodats.v12i1.05.
sources.note: Nothing: no tone or stress statement for any variety (the only 'stress' string is in a reference title about English stress); the 'phonological processes' are syncope, apocope, metathesis and sound correspondences between the three Kuteb dialects; wordlist items are given without tone marks.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2005. Is there a boundary between Plateau and Jukunoid? Draft paper for the Vienna Jukunoid workshop, 19-20 Nov 2005
sources.note: Zero mentions of Kapya (a full-text search for stress/accent count 0). Sec. 2.3 Tones is about Plateau vs Jukunoid tone systems ('four and five-tone systems characteristic of some Jukunoid languages'); no stress. Sec. 1.3.2 lists the Jukunoid data sources (Shimizu 1980a,b; Dykstra n.d; Priest & Priest n.d; Koops 1990, n.d; Storch; Vienna project).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record kapy1238 (Hammarström et al.), incl. 'meds' list and reference records 714024, 302077, 309353
sources.note: No descriptive work with a phonology of Kapya. Most-extensive descriptions: Prischnegg 2008 (whose fullest description per Glottolog is a phonology or text collection, 30 pp bearing on Kapya) and R. Koops 1994 'The sounds of Kapya --- tentative analysis', 6 pp, unpublished ms (ref 714024, whose fullest description per Glottolog is only a wordlist). Neither online.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2026. Rethinking the classification of 'South Jukunoid'. Paper, Third Conference on Bantoid Languages and Linguistics (Bantoid 3), University at Buffalo, 20-21 May 2026.
sources.note: Comparative/classificatory paper; most recent treatment with Kapya data (Blench proposes a Kuteb–Kapya branch); likely contains a Kapya wordlist with tone marks and a note on data sources (possibly Koops 1994). academia.edu 403 and rogerblench.info captcha-blocked for us.

sources.citation: Kempf, Viktoria & Tamara Prischnegg. 2020. A sketch of Akum (Southern Jukunoid). Afrika und Übersee 93: 298-326. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.215
sources.note: Nothing about Kapya beyond naming it as a Southern Jukunoid member (p. 305: 'the whole Southern Jukunoid language group (Bezen, Bete, Lufu, Akum, Kuteb, Yukuben, Kapya)'). Its phonology section (2.3 Tone, p. 306) describes AKUM: 'Akum has a three-tone system.. we only find lexically distinctive tones'; no stress statement for any language.

sources.citation: Endangered Languages Project / ELCat entry 4406 'Kapya' (main page and bibliography), the Internet Archive copies 2015/2019
sources.note: Nothing; bibliography consists only of Ethnologue 16 (2009) and the World Oral Literature Project; 'No documents have been added'. Classification Jukunoid, Yukuben-Kuteb; 200 speakers (2004).

sources.citation: Lewis, M. Paul, Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds.). 2013. Ethnologue 17, entry 'Kapya' (Internet Archive copy 2014); also Ethnologue 24 (2021) paywalled shell
sources.note: Nothing on phonology. 'Population 200 (2004). Location Taraba State, Takum LGA, at Kapya. Language Status 6b (Threatened). Dialects Related to Kutep [kub].'

sources.citation: Prischnegg, Tamara (data) in Chan, Eugene S. L. (comp.). 2013. 'Kapya'. sources.note: Kuteb is Kapya's closest relative (Ethnologue: 'Related to Kutep'; Blench 2026: Kuteb–Kapya branch); its phonology chapter is the nearest full description of the prosodic type, and the introduction may mention Koops's own Kapya sketch. Not a Kapya statement itself.
